note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 2863 / 出力 1681 トークン

data.question: Should hold_limit be raised from 70s to 80s, which narrows the utility spread between companies but lowers the worst company's on-time rate from 0.97 to 0.94?
data.background: The proposal passes check and the constitution, improves the main goal (utility_gap) by +1.6 on 4/5 seeds, and has a quorum (B and C yes, A no). It still conflicts with the other KPI goals: min_company_on_time_rate, on-time deliveries and late deliveries all get worse. Weighing company fairness against service to customers is a value judgement the KPI does not settle, and customers have no vote, so a human should decide.

options.summary: Adopt hold_limit 80s. Utility_gap improves by +1.6 (utility A / B / C goes from 26.8 / 25.6 / 11.2 to 26.0 / 25.2 / 12.0). On-time deliveries go from 85.6 to 85.0, late deliveries from 1.8 to 2.4, the lowest on-time rate from 0.97 to 0.94 (still above the 0.9 floor), blocked seconds from 976 to 1111, and road violations from 27.2 to 25.6. Seeds improved: 4/5.
options.stakeholders: C gains (+0.8 utility). A loses (-0.8) and votes no. B loses slightly (-0.4) but votes yes. Customers lose a little: about 0.6 more late deliveries and 0.6 fewer on-time deliveries, with the worst-served company's customers seeing on-time fall to 0.94. Part of the narrower spread comes from lowering A and B, not only from raising C.

options.summary: Stay at v3 (hold_limit 70s). Utility_gap stays at the current spread (26.8 / 25.6 / 11.2), with 85.6 on-time, 1.8 late, lowest on-time rate 0.97 and 976 blocked seconds.
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the current, slightly better service. A keeps its higher utility. C stays far behind A and B, which weakens the cooperation goal of the quiet-season KPI. B and C's yes votes would not be acted on.

recommendation.reason: The quiet-season KPI makes utility_gap the main goal. The gain is consistent (4/5 seeds), the 0.9 floor that you set to stop the spread being narrowed by worse service still holds with margin (0.94), and the change has a quorum without an override. It continues the direction you adopted in D5. The service cost to customers is small but real, so I suggest re-measuring the lowest on-time rate and late deliveries next period and reverting if they keep falling toward 0.9.

unknowns: Which company's on-time rate falls to 0.94, and whose customers bear the extra late deliveries
Why A votes no, and whether A would reduce cooperation if outvoted
How customers perceive a small rise in late deliveries during the quiet season
Order volume next period, and whether the trade-off holds if demand rises again
Why the one remaining seed did not improve, and how large the variance across seeds is
Whether raising hold_limit again (after the D5 change from 60s to 70s) has cumulative effects on blocking that were not measured, such as the rise to 1111 blocked seconds
